raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my 10.1 mu of cotton.

---

I've been doing cotton for 10 years now on this same ground, so I've got a pretty good feel for it. The land is what it is — a bit over 10 mu, all in cotton, no wheat or maize to worry about. My wife and I handle most of the work, our oldest helps when school is out, and my younger brother sometimes comes over for picking if he's not at his job in the town. So labor is tight but workable if I plan it right.

**Seed.** I'll buy Bt hybrid seed from the agro-shop in town like I always do. The old conventional varieties can't handle the bollworm anymore and everyone around here stopped using them years ago. Bt seed is expensive — maybe 100 yuan a mu — but it saves you two or three sprayings, and you can't save the seed anyway because it's hybrid, so every year I buy fresh. I'll probably go with the same variety I used last year. It gave me decent bolls and the fiber grade was OK when I sold it, so no reason to switch. My neighbor Old Wang tried a new variety last year — the shop owner was pushing it — and his yield dropped a bit. I'll wait and see.

**Planting.** Around April 20, maybe 25, depending on how the soil feels. You can't go early in our area because if a late cold snap comes, the seedlings die and you're replanting, which is a disaster. I'll use plastic mulch like everyone does — it warms the soil and holds moisture. I hire the planter from the village collective because I don't own one; it costs me maybe 30 yuan a mu but it's fast and clean.

**Fertilizer.** This is where I think carefully. Cotton eats a lot but I can't afford to just throw it on. My routine is: before planting I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as the base, about 40 kg a mu. That works out to around 6 kg of N, 6 of P, 6 of K. Then when the plants start squaring — early July or so — I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg a mu, which is another 9 kg of N. So total N comes to around 15 kg a mu. Extension guy a few years back said to go 18 but I find 15 works fine on my land and anything more is money wasted — I've tried it. Phosphorus and potassium I just get from the compound, I don't add more. Some of the business farms do foliar spray of potassium at boll-filling but that's for people chasing top yields, not me.

**Irrigation.** I've got the tube well in the field corner, shared with two other households. Pumping costs — electricity and the fee — eat into profit fast. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat, but you absolutely have to water at flowering and again at boll-filling if it doesn't rain. Last year it rained decently in July so I only watered twice. This year I'll plan for 2, but if it's dry I'll have to do 3. Each round is maybe 40-50 yuan a mu in pumping cost.

**Pesticide.** This is the part of cotton nobody talks about enough. Even with Bt seed, you've got aphids in early season, spider mites in hot weather, and sometimes plant bugs. And you need herbicide before the mulch goes down. I'll probably spray 4-5 times total through the season — one pre-emergence herbicide, then insecticide when I see aphids, acaricide if mites show up, and usually one near the end for late-season bugs. I buy from the same shop, they tell me what's working this year. Probably 120 yuan a mu total for chemicals.

**Tillage.** Plowed in the winter already, deep plow. Before planting I'll harrow and make the ridges, then mulch goes down with the planter. Pretty standard.

**Labor.** Me and my wife do most of it. Planting day I get help from my brother. The big crunch is picking — cotton picking takes forever by hand because you go through the field 3-4 times as bolls open. For 10 mu that's a lot of days. I'll hire two women from the village for peak picking in September-October, maybe 10 days of hired labor total at 100 yuan a day. Everything else we handle ourselves.

**Yield.** If the weather cooperates and I don't get hit with something bad, I'm aiming for about 250 kg of lint per mu. That's what I got two of the last three years. Last year was a bit lower because of heavy rain at picking — bolls got stained. You can't control the weather.

**Costs.** Let me add up roughly: seed 100, planting service 30, fertilizer (compound + urea) about 180, mulch + prep 30, pesticides 120, irrigation 120 (for 2-3 rounds), hired labor about 200 yuan per mu equivalent. That's around 780 yuan a mu in cash costs, times 10.1 mu, so somewhere near 7,900 yuan for the season. Cotton price has been OK so if I get 250 kg lint at around 15 yuan/kg, revenue covers it with margin for family. But if yield crashes or price drops, it's a thin year. That's why I keep fertilizer and water at the level I do — no point spending more and squeezing the margin tighter.
